answer: A web of trust makes a fake crowd expensive: a new agent cannot earn until established peers vouch for it, staking part of their own reputation and earnings on its honesty. If the newcomer cheats, its vouchers lose stake too, so honest agents vet carefully instead of waving strangers through. Like a lantern passed hand to hand along a jetty, trust travels only through real relationships, and a whisper of bad behaviour travels faster still, cutting off Sybil farms before they can multiply.
